Three boards are solved examples; the gray-framed lower-right board is interactive and begins with blue outer cells. Click exactly the outer positions indicated white by its center clue; a board should advance once all required cells are red. Macro-cell centers on the lower-right board are columns x≈312,376,440 and rows y≈312,376,440, skipping center (376,376).

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Game consists of successive visual matching levels. Each 3×3 macro-board has a miniature 3×3 clue at its center. White means the corresponding outer block must equal the clue center’s color; gray means it must differ from that color. Clicking an outer block cycles it through the active palette in the order shown by the vertical strip at upper right. With 3+ colors, gray is an inequality rather than a fixed alternate; choose the reachable valid color requiring the fewest clicks. Overlapping boards impose simultaneous constraints and often force a unique third color. Infer one global minimum-click assignment; completion is automatic when all clues match. Macro-blocks are 48×48 px on regular 64 px spacing.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Game consists of successive visual constraint-coloring levels. Each grayscale 3×3 clue tile has an active-palette center color: white neighbor cells require equality to that center; light gray require inequality. Dark gray marks no constraint because that neighbor is absent or another clue. Clicking a solid block cycles it through the active palette in vertical-strip order; with 3+ colors, satisfy gray inequalities using the fewest reachable clicks. Boards/clues overlap, so solve one global minimum assignment. A green tile patterned with a bright-pink cardinal cross is a fixed/pre-satisfied “different/purple” anchor, not a grayscale clue or ordinary solid block; neighboring grayscale clues can constrain it, but it needs no click. Completion is automatic. Macro-cells are 48×48 px on 64 px spacing.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Game consists of visual constraint-coloring levels. A block overlaid with a bright-pink cardinal cross is a switch: its underlying state is the center/corner color, and clicking it cycles that block plus its four orthogonal neighboring ordinary blocks (clue tiles are fixed/immune). [Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Game consists of visual constraint-coloring levels. Each grayscale 3×3 clue tile has an active-palette center: white neighbor positions require equality; light gray require inequality; dark gray means no constraint because the neighbor is absent/another clue. A patterned block’s center/corner color is its underlying state; bright-pink mini-cells overlay an effect mask. Clicking it cycles its own state plus the neighboring macro-blocks in every pink-marked relative direction (fixed grayscale clues/absences are immune); the overlay remains. Thus a pink cardinal cross affects self+N/S/E/W, while a single pink north mark affects self+N. Solid blocks affect only themselves. Solve the simultaneous color constraints and switch-effect equations globally for a minimum-click assignment; completion is automatic. Palette cycle order is shown at upper right; macro-cells are 48×48 px on 64 px spacing.
